questions.stem: Find the angle between the hands of a clock at \(10:10\).
questions.keySolution:
At \(10:10\):
Minute hand position = \(10 × 6 = 60°\) from 12
Hour hand position = \(10 × 30 + 10 × 0.5 = 305.0°\) from 12
Angle = \(|305.0 - 60| = 115.0°\)

questions.stem: Between \(9\) and \(10\) o'clock, the hour hand and minute hand will be perpendicular (at right angles). Find the approximate time.
questions.keySolution:
For perpendicular hands between hour H and H+1, use formula:
M = (2/11)[30H ± 90]
For hour \(9\):
M = (2/11)[30(9) ± 90] = (2/11)[270 ± 90]
This gives approximately \(32\) minutes past \(9\)

questions.stem: Between \(8\) and \(9\) o'clock, at what time will the hour hand and minute hand be in opposite directions (\(180°\) apart)?
questions.keySolution:
For opposite hands between hour H and H+1, use:
Angle = \(|30H - 5.5M| = 180\)
Solving: M = (2/11)(30H ± 180)
For hour \(8\), this gives approximately \(10\) minutes

questions.stem: At what time between \(7\) and \(8\) o'clock will the angle between the hands be \(150°\)?
questions.keySolution:
Using formula: M = (2/11)(30H ± A), where A = \(150°\)
M = (2/11)(30(7) ± 150)
M = (2/11) × 210 ± (2/11) × 150
This gives approximately \(11\) minutes past \(7\) o'clock.

questions.stem: By \(11:45\), how many degrees will the minute hand turn from the initial position (starting from 12:00)?
questions.keySolution:
The minute hand moves \(0.5°\) per minute for hour hand and \(6°\) per minute for minute hand.
Total time = \(11\) hours \(45\) minutes = \(705\) minutes
Angle traced by minute hand = \(705 × 6 = 270°\)
